edits.old: Distinguish application-cache stampedes from WiredTiger page eviction. WiredTiger normally evicts pages to free cache space; under pressure application threads can perform eviction, diverting time from operations and increasing latency. Eviction activity alone does not establish a self-sustaining death spiral. (high confidence)
edits.new: WiredTiger continuously evicts pages to free cache space. When its eviction threads cannot keep up with demand for cache space, application threads are tasked with eviction as well, throttling operations and increasing latency (default trigger 95% of cache). Whether eviction activity alone indicates a self-sustaining death spiral is an interpretive judgment, not stated by WiredTiger documentation. Sources: https://source.wiredtiger.com/develop/eviction.html ; https://source.wiredtiger.com/11.3.1/tune_cache.html

evidence.quote: WiredTiger has to continuously move data that is currently not being accessed out of the memory to free up enough space to read data that are requested by the user

Finally, if the Wiredtiger eviction threads are unable to keep up with application demand for cache space, application threads will be tasked with eviction as well, potentially resulting in latency spikes.
The eviction_trigger configuration value (default 95%) is the level at which application threads start to perform eviction. This will throttle application operations, increasing operation latency

edits.old: Exercise real retry behavior and dependency failure under load. Delayed responses waste work after deadlines, and retries amplify demand; backoff and jitter reduce synchronization but do not guarantee recovery from global overload. (high confidence)
edits.new: Exercise real retry behavior and dependency failure under load. Work finished after the client has timed out is wasted, and retries multiply offered load (exponentially across deep call graphs). Randomized backoff keeps retries from synchronizing, but when retries keep an overloaded backend overloaded, recovery requires dramatically reducing or eliminating load until the retries stop. Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/ ; https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/

evidence.quote: Otherwise, the server keeps working on the request, and its late reply is like a tree falling in the forest.

in order to dig out of this outage, you must dramatically reduce or eliminate the load on the frontends until the retries stop and the backends stabilize.
